candidates.excerpt: NEW HAVEN, Ind. — The Pennsylvania Railroad T1 Steam Locomotive Trust announced the acquisition of two former Pennsylvania Railroad E8A diesel locomotives from the Fort Wayne Railroad Historical Society. Built in September and November 1952, respectively, Nos. 5702A and 5761A faced an uncertain future as the assets of the former Iowa Pacific Holdings were dispersed across the country following the company’s collapse. Members of the Fort Wayne Railroad Historical Society stepped forward in 2021 to acquire and safeguard the locomotives. “Over the past five years, several long-term preservation opportunities were evaluated as the organization stewarded over $40,000 in storage costs sponsored by a private donor,” the press release said. The same donor financed the sale of the locomotives to the T1 Trust. Hunt Transport Services Inc. today reported solid third-quarter intermodal growth while signaling that higher rates can be expected in the immediate future as the company tries to close the growing gap between truck and rail pricing. The largest domestic intermodal provider said volume increased 8% over last year, to 585,582 loads for the quarter. However, the pace of growth was slower than the 10% increase in the second quarter. Intermodal volume rose 18% in J.B. Hunt’s Eastern network, reflecting very tight truckload carrier capacity in the region, Darren Field, president of intermodal, told analysts and investors on the company’s earnings call. In contrast, transcon intermodal rose 1% in a market where Hunt competes less against highway carriers and more against all-water and international intermodal service. The volume improvement at J.B. Container lines, sensing a gradual slowdown in Indian westbound volumes, are revisiting their surcharges and penalties, indicating a hot market may be turning decidedly cooler. The German carrier reportedly had the highest such charge among the major carriers, sparking concerns for Indian exporters as they scrambled for vessel space. candidates.excerpt: South Korea’s HMM is pressing ahead with its fleet expansion programme, approving a $1.62bn investment in 12 containerships comprising eight 13,000 teu newbuildings and four smaller vessels. The Seoul-listed carrier’s board approved spending KRW2.168trn ($1.617bn) yesterday, according to a stock exchange filing. The investment includes fresh orders for eight 13,000 teu ships, alongside the acquisition of three 2,800 teu vessels and one 1,700 teu ship through resale transactions involving newbuildings already under construction. The 12 vessels will add a combined 114,100 teu of capacity, with deliveries scheduled to be completed by December 2029. HMM has yet to identify the shipyards responsible for the eight larger vessels or the sellers of the four smaller ships. Propulsion specifications have also not been disclosed. candidates.excerpt: Record monthly container volumes at Port of Long Beach as imports soar The US West Coast gateway port saw the ratio of imports to exports exceed 5:1 in September The Port of Long Beach (POLB) handled close to 1 million teu in the month of September a 25% increase year-on-year. The Californian port handled 997,177 teu in September eclipsing the previous monthly record of 987,191 teu in October 2024. The port credited the record volume number to an inclusion shippers’ cost-saving strategies against high diesel costs, Panama Canal access restrictions and a possible new US - China trade deal. Imports fuelled September’s throughput at the Port of Long Beach with a 31.3% jump to 509,390 teu compared to the same month in 2025. The surge in imports see the ratio of import to export boxes exceeding 5:1 with the port handling 91,747 teu of exports. candidates.excerpt: A state agency is providing a $1 million loan to add a rail spur connecting the Port of Columbia to Union Pacific’s main line. Louisiana Economic Development awarded the loan under its FastSites program, helping close a funding gap on the $7 million project. The port, on a 400-acre site, has direct access to the Ouachita River and U.S. Route 165, and is adjacent to UP’s (NYSE: UNP)Monroe Subdivision. candidates.excerpt: Massachusetts Governor Maura Healey’s administration announced a major step toward permanent seasonal Berkshire Flyer service and expanded passenger rail in Western Massachusetts. An agreement between the Massachusetts Department of Transportation (MassDOT) and CSX will advance critical rail infrastructure improvements in Pittsfield that will reduce conflicts between passenger and freight trains and support permanent seasonal Berkshire Flyer service. The administration also announced that new federal funding awarded to Amtrak for additional modern trainsets will support Compass Rail services, including the Berkshire Flyer and the future Inland Route between Boston, Springfield and New Haven.
